facts: Each of the actual four common root processors first checks object type and presence of its own named root member before selecting that child.

The popup processor also has an existing request-path exclusion; the mission processor performs its existing path/regex setup and exclusion before its guarded JSON update. No new routes are inferred from those exclusions.
An empty object contains none of these four keys, so their child parsers and corresponding model mutations are not entered.
The support-memory update reads current/prev only if support_memory_enhancements exists. The score-benefit boolean conversion is only reached if is_score_benefits_unlocked exists.
All four decompilation instruction footprints stay within their declared bodies. No new body or test was needed for the already-reviewed common member-presence helper.
limits: This is static optional-field behavior, not proof that an arbitrary endpoint accepts an empty object. Each endpoint success consumer must be proved separately.
Missing optional updates preserve model state; this proof does not grant mission, popup, support-memory or score-benefit state.
The ordinary wrapper still runs its existing generic processing and endpoint callback. No UI, gameplay, native execution or package build is claimed.
